content: 1. Lemborexant: Cimetidine can increase the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 2. Levoketoconazole: Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Lidocaine: Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Cimetidine and Lomitapide: Lomitapide increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Consider reducing the cimetidine dose when used concomitantly with lomitapide. 5. Cimetidine and Lomustine: Cimetidine decreases the metabolism of lomustine, potentially enhancing myelotoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Lonafarnib: Lonafarnib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor, and co-administration with P-gp substrates may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Reduce the P-gp substrate dose if necessary. 7. Lurasidone: Cimetidine increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. The manufacturer recommends reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. 8. Mavacamten: Cimetidine increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 9. Mavorixafor: Mavorixafor increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with sensitive P-gp substrates may lead to serious adverse effects. 10. Mebendazole: Cimetidine increases mebendazole levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Mefloquine: Cimetidine increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Melatonin: Cimetidine increases melatonin levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor melatonin effects when co-administered with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors. 13. Memantine: Cimetidine increases memantine levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Metformin: Cimetidine increases metformin levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Methamphetamine: Cimetidine increases methamphetamine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Methylphenidate: Cimetidine decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), co-administration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Consider separating the administration of the antacid and methylphenidate. 17. Metoprolol: Cimetidine increases metoprolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Mexiletine: Cimetidine increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting both CYP1A2 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Midazolam (Intranasal): Cimetidine increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Midodrine: Cimetidine increases midodrine levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Mizolastine: Cimetidine increases mizolastine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Momelotinib: Momelotinib increases cimetidine toxicity by competing for plasma protein binding. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Dose adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. 23. Morphine: Cimetidine increases morphine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Nateglinide: Cimetidine increases nateglinide levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Nebivolol: Cimetidine increases nebivolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Nelfinavir: Cimetidine increases nelfinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Nicotine (Inhaled and Intranasal): Cimetidine increases nicotine levels by decreasing renal clearance and metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Nifedipine: Cimetidine increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Nilotinib: Cimetidine decreases nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Avoid this interaction by administering H2 antagonists 10 hours after or 2 hours before nilotinib. 30. Nimodipine: Cimetidine increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Nortriptyline: Cimetidine increases nortriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Olanzapine: Cimetidine increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Oliceridine: Cimetidine increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. If co-administration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 34. Oxybutynin: Cimetidine increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Oxycodone: Cimetidine increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Oxymorphone: Cimetidine increases oxymorphone levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Paclitaxel: Cimetidine increases paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Palbociclib: Cimetidine increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Paroxetine: Cimetidine increases paroxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Pentoxifylline: Cimetidine increases pentoxifylline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Phenytoin: Cimetidine increases phenytoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Pimozide: Cimetidine increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Pioglitazone: Cimetidine increases pioglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Polysaccharide Iron: Cimetidine decreases polysaccharide iron levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Ponatinib: Ponatinib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Posaconazole: Cimetidine decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Pramipexole: Cimetidine increases pramipexole levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Praziquantel: Cimetidine increases praziquantel levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Propranolol: Cimetidine increases propranolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Quinine: Cimetidine increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Ramelteon: Cimetidine increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Rasagiline: Cimetidine increases rasagiline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
